headline: Germany's Bundeswehr Voluntary Service 2026: New Law, Pay and How to Join
metaDescription: Germany's voluntary military service 2026: 6-23 month terms, ~€2,600/month pay, age 17+, German citizenship required. New Wehrdienst law: benefits, Musterung.

sections.content:
On 1 January 2026, Germany's new military service law took effect, keeping the voluntary model instead of returning to conscription. The reform responds to a personnel shortage: the Bundeswehr aims to grow toward roughly 260,000 active soldiers by 2035, with an additional 200,000 reservists planned.

All 18-year-old men receive a mandatory online questionnaire about fitness, skills and interest; from July 2027 they also face a compulsory medical examination. Women may participate voluntarily. If voluntary enlistment falls short of targets, parliament could vote on a needs-based conscription – a decision that would require new legislation.
sections.title: The New Military Service Law 2026

sections.content:
Volunteers earn a gross monthly pay of about 2,600 euros for a minimum six-month term, including free accommodation, food and medical care. Those serving at least twelve months receive a subsidy of up to 3,500 euros toward a car driving licence, or up to 5,000 euros for a truck licence.

The first six months count as a probation period with the right to leave at any time. Service time counts as a waiting semester for university admission, and a confirmed study place is kept. Longer commitments open access to advanced training and career-soldier contracts.
sections.title: Pay, Benefits and Incentives

sections.content:
Applicants must be German citizens, at least 17 years old, and pass the medical examination (Musterung). The voluntary service lasts between 6 and 23 months, chosen freely, and interested candidates can apply through the Bundeswehr career centers or the online application portal.

Those committing to twelve months or more may continue as temporary career soldiers (Soldat auf Zeit) with pay under the federal pay scale, earning around 2,700 euros gross monthly in the lowest grade. Assignments are placed near home whenever possible.
sections.title: Eligibility and How to Apply

sections.content:
After service, volunteers can transition to longer Bundeswehr contracts, enter the reserves, or move into civilian careers with documented skills. The military also offers funded vocational and university education for longer-serving personnel.

For those unsure about a military career, the reform also strengthened civilian alternatives: the Federal Voluntary Service receives additional funding and over 15,000 new positions in areas like education, eldercare and disaster relief.
